# Vibe Pipeline

Turn one project idea into the complete asset set for LLM-driven development, in five gated stages. Two tracks share the same gates:

```
UI track:     S1 PRD.md (or other doc) → S2 architecture.md → S3 mockup.html (+ images/) → S4 storyboard.md  → S5 vibe-prompts/
non-UI track: S1 Technical Proposal (or other doc) → S2 architecture.md → S3 skeleton/ (runnable stubs) → S4 walkthrough.md → S5 vibe-prompts/
```

The non-UI track is for projects with no user interface: scripts, CLI tools, downloaders/scrapers, data pipelines, analyses whose output is documents/data.

Each stage's output is the context for the next, so quality compounds — and so do mistakes. That is why the review gates below are not optional.

## The one rule that governs everything

**Never generate two stages in one turn.** After writing each artifact, stop and hand control back to the user with the checkpoint message (see "Checkpoint protocol"). Only proceed to the next stage after the user explicitly approves. If the user says "just do it all," explain that downstream artifacts are built on upstream ones, so a five-minute review of the PRD saves an hour of regenerating everything else — then still pause at each gate unless they insist again after that explanation.

## Stage 0 — Intake & entry point

The pipeline does NOT assume you start from scratch. First determine where to begin.

### Step 0a — Scan for existing artifacts

Before asking anything, check the project directory (and read `vibe-pipeline-state.md` if it exists) for any of these:

| Stage | UI track | non-UI track |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | `PRD.md` | `technical-proposal.md` (or other S1 doc) |
| S2 | `architecture.md` | `architecture.md` |
| S3 | `mockup.html`, `images/` | `skeleton/` |
| S4 | `storyboard.md` | `walkthrough.md` |
| S5 | `vibe-prompts/` | `vibe-prompts/` |

Which files exist also reveals the track a previous session chose (also recorded in `vibe-pipeline-state.md`).

Also honor an **explicit entry point** in the user's message or `goes straight to vibe codign prompt for these features: 1. zoom in and out on the map; 2. move around on the map; 3. when grid cell is clicked, zoom in to that location. remember to add bash script at the end. goal of the bash script is for me to be able to manually check what was being built. bash script is not for running the test written automatically.` — e.g. "I have the PRD, generate the architecture" or "modify the mockup". An explicit instruction always wins over auto-detection.

Then report what you found and propose a starting point, e.g.:

> Found `PRD.md` and `architecture.md` on disk; no mockup yet. I can start at **S3 (mockup)** and treat the two existing files as approved context. Or point me somewhere else.

### Step 0b — Validate brought-in artifacts

Any artifact that exists on disk but the skill didn't generate this session (no matching `approved` line in `vibe-pipeline-state.md`) is a **brought-in** file. Before building anything on top of it:

1. Read it and check it against its reference template (`references/<stage>-template.md`) for the structure/fields downstream stages depend on.
2. If it's missing something important, tell the user what's thin (e.g. "your PRD has no User Flows section, which S4 needs") and offer to patch it or proceed as-is.
3. Present it at that stage's checkpoint as a draft to **approve as the baseline**. Only after approval does it count as context for later stages. This means a brought-in file is treated exactly like a generated draft — the user can `approve`, `revise:`, or hand-edit it first.

### Step 0c — Modifying an existing artifact

If the user wants to change an artifact they already have (generated or brought-in), route it through that stage as a `revise:` (see Checkpoint protocol): rework only that artifact, then **mark every downstream artifact stale** and offer to regenerate them in order, gate by gate. Example: editing the mockup at S3 makes `storyboard.md` (S4) and `vibe-prompts/` (S5) stale, because the screens and the build prompts were derived from the old mockup.

### Step 0d — Track & S1 document type (always establish, ask if not stated)

Before intake, establish two things. If the user's message already answers them, confirm in passing rather than re-asking; otherwise ask both together in one short message:

1. **What should the S1 document be?** Default suggestions: **PRD** (products/apps) or **Technical Proposal** (scripts, tools, automation, analyses). If the user names anything else — "Analysis Plan", "Migration Plan", "Research Protocol" — adapt the closest bundled template to that type (see the note in `references/technical-proposal-template.md`); never refuse because a type isn't listed. The chosen name becomes the S1 filename in kebab-case (e.g. `technical-proposal.md`, `analysis-plan.md`).
2. **Is a UI/UX needed?** This selects the track. For mixed cases (e.g. mostly a CLI tool but with a small dashboard), don't guess — lay out the difference (mockup + storyboard vs. skeleton + walkthrough) and let the user pick; a mostly-UI project usually wants the UI track, a script with incidental UI usually wants the non-UI track with the small UI handled as one feature phase in S5.

Record both answers (track + S1 doc type) in `vibe-pipeline-state.md`.

### Step 0e — Intake questions

Only when starting at S1 (or when a brought-in file lacks context) gather what's missing:

1. **App idea** (required) — what it does and why
2. Target users
3. Must-have features for v1
4. Tech stack preference (if none, the architecture stage decides)
5. Any constraints or notes

Ask only for what's missing; the idea alone is enough to start if the user prefers. If entering at a later stage, you can infer most of this from the approved upstream artifacts — don't re-interrogate the user for things the PRD already answers.

All artifacts go in the project root (plus an `images/` folder). Record intake answers and entry point at the top of `vibe-pipeline-state.md` so later sessions can resume.

## Stages 1–5

For each stage, read its reference file **before writing the artifact** — it contains the required structure and quality bar:

| Stage | UI track artifact | non-UI track artifact | Reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | `PRD.md` | `technical-proposal.md` (or the doc type chosen in 0d) | `references/prd-template.md` / `references/technical-proposal-template.md` |
| S2 | `architecture.md` | `architecture.md` | `references/architecture-template.md` |
| S3 | `mockup.html` + `images/` | `skeleton/` — runnable stub code | `references/mockup-spec.md` / `references/skeleton-spec.md` |
| S4 | `storyboard.md` | `walkthrough.md` | `references/storyboard-template.md` / `references/walkthrough-template.md` |
| S5 | `vibe-prompts/` folder — `00-README.md` + one standalone prompt file per atomic phase | same | `references/vibe-prompt-template.md` |

Read the reference for the track you're on. The S1 clarify step below applies to whichever S1 document was chosen.

Context per stage: the intake answers plus **every previously approved artifact** (read them from disk — do not rely on conversation memory, which may be stale or compacted).

### S1 — clarify before writing the PRD

The PRD is the root of the whole pipeline, so a wrong assumption here propagates into every later artifact. Before writing `PRD.md`, review the intake and ask clarifying questions **only where a genuine ambiguity would change the PRD** — don't interrogate the user for its own sake. Good triggers for a question: the core user action or primary flow is unclear, "must-have features" are vague or seem to exceed a lean v1, the target user is undefined, there's an implied auth/payments/data-sensitivity dimension the user hasn't addressed, or the platform (web/mobile/desktop) isn't obvious.

Guidelines:
- Batch questions into one short round (aim for 3–6, grouped), not a slow back-and-forth. Prefer concrete either/or options over open prompts, e.g. "Auth: (a) email+password, (b) social login, (c) none for v1?"
- For anything the user leaves unanswered or says "you decide," make a reasonable assumption, **state it explicitly in the PRD** (an "Assumptions" note), and move on — never block.
- If the intake is already detailed and unambiguous, skip straight to drafting; say so briefly rather than manufacturing questions.
- Skip this step when entering at S2+ with an approved/brought-in PRD already in hand — that PRD is the source of truth; raise concerns as revise suggestions instead.

Record any material answers in `vibe-pipeline-state.md` alongside the intake so a later session has them.

### S3 → S4, UI track — screen capture, then reference (this chain is the point)

The storyboard must show the *actual* mockup screens, and the build prompts must point at those same images, so the final app looks exactly like the approved storyboard. Enforce this three-link chain:

1. **Extract (end of S3).** After the user approves `mockup.html`, run `scripts/screenshot-mockup.mjs` to render each `[data-screen]` container into `images/screen-NN-<name>.png`, numbered in DOM order. The script needs Node 18+ and **auto-installs Playwright and its Chromium browser on first run** if they're missing (one-time, ~150 MB download for the browser) — no need to ask permission for a normal run, though mention the one-time install is happening. If the environment blocks the download and the script exits with an install error, fall back to having the user open `mockup.html` and capture each screen manually using those exact filenames. Either way, do not enter S4 until `images/` is populated — confirm the files exist first.

2. **Reference (in S4).** `storyboard.md` embeds each captured file by its real path (`![Screen Name](./images/screen-NN-<name>.png)`) next to that screen's written journey. Derive the screen list and filenames from what's actually in `images/` (list the folder — don't guess names), so every embed resolves to a real file.

3. **Carry forward (in S5).** Each relevant phase prompt in `vibe-prompts/` references the specific `images/screen-NN-*.png` files for the screens it builds, and instructs the model to match them, so the implemented UI reproduces the storyboard rather than reinventing it.

If the mockup changes later, re-run the extract step so the images stay in sync before regenerating `storyboard.md`.

### S3 → S4, non-UI track — runnable skeleton, then walkthrough

Same principle, different medium: the user reviews the *shape* of the program before any business logic exists, and the build prompts implement exactly that shape.

1. **Skeleton (S3).** Build `skeleton/` per `references/skeleton-spec.md`: real code files in the S2-chosen language, every module and public function present with final signatures, docstrings stating the behavior contract, bodies returning realistic mock data or raising NotImplementedError tagged with the implementing phase, and a wired entry point. **Run the entry point and show the output at the checkpoint** — the skeleton must execute end-to-end on mock data. (No screenshot step on this track; Playwright is not needed.)
2. **Walkthrough (S4).** Write `walkthrough.md` per `references/walkthrough-template.md`: Mermaid + ASCII execution schematic, one section per step referencing the **exact stub signatures from skeleton/** (read the files, don't guess), input→output per step, failure paths, and an end-to-end trace of a mock run.
3. **Carry forward (S5).** Phase prompts implement the stub bodies feature-by-feature **without changing the reviewed signatures**; each phase names the exact files/functions it fills in (see the template's Skeleton Reference section).

If the skeleton changes later (signatures added/renamed), regenerate `walkthrough.md` before S5, same staleness rule as the UI track.

## Checkpoint protocol

After writing each artifact, output exactly this shape of message and stop:

> **✅ S<N> draft ready: `<filename>`**
> Summary: <2–3 bullets of the key decisions made in this artifact>
> Open it and review. Then tell me one of:
> - **approve** — I'll continue to S<N+1> (<next artifact>)
> - **revise: <your notes>** — I'll rework this draft
> - or edit the file yourself and say **approve** when done

For a **brought-in** artifact (existed on disk, not generated this session), the checkpoint says "approve as baseline" instead of drafting from scratch — the user confirms the existing file is good to build on, or `revise:`s it first.

On "revise": rework only the current artifact per the notes, then checkpoint again.
On approval of an artifact that has approved **downstream** artifacts (the user went back, or modified an earlier stage): warn that downstream artifacts are now stale and offer to regenerate them in order, gate by gate. If the modified stage was the mockup, re-run the S3 screenshot extraction before regenerating the storyboard.

## Stage tracking

Maintain `vibe-pipeline-state.md` in the project root: intake answers, plus one line per stage (`S1 PRD.md — approved 2026-07-05`, `S3 — draft, awaiting review`, `S4 — stale (S2 revised)`). Update it at every checkpoint. This file is how a fresh session resumes mid-pipeline.

## What this skill is NOT for

Do not use this skill to implement the app itself. The pipeline ends at the `vibe-prompts/` folder. If the user asks to start building, that's a normal coding session driven by the generated phase prompts, not this skill.
